correctness.rationale: Support cells \(C_S\) have size \(w(S)\), contain no internal edges, and are completely joined exactly for disjoint supports. Maximum independent sets therefore saturate selected cells. Complementary pairs yield the upper bound. Positive values \(b_i=\log(q_i-1)\) prove that all strict-heavy supports and arbitrary one-per-pair tied choices are pairwise intersecting, giving equality and classifying all maximizers. The alternative absolute-difference formula follows by summing \(\max(u,v)=(u+v+|u-v|)/2\). Exhaustive small-rank verification agrees with these conclusions.

value.rationale: Exact independence numbers and maximum independent sets are natural invariants for zero-divisor graphs, and the direct prior paper devotes separate theorems to factor counts three, four, and five. The accepted theorem removes that bounded-rank casework for every nonbinary finite-field product, classifies all maximizers, counts them by a tie statistic, and identifies why binary factors are the sharp obstruction to the proof mechanism.
